pages.text: "No bath! It stings my eyes!" Pipo backed away from the big wooden tub in the yard. Mom poured water. "Pipo, time to wash." He shook his head and fled to the shed.
Pipo buried himself in hay. "No bath! I will sleep here today!" Only his scarf tip stuck out. Mom smiled a little and finished filling the tub.
But the hay felt scratchy and itchy. After a day's running, bits of hay stuck to his sweaty fur. "Oh? Why is my fur so sticky?" He scratched his side.
Mom brought soap and a water bucket to the shed. "Pipo, instead of a bath, want to make a bubble mountain?" His head poked out. "A bubble mountain? What is that?"
Mom mixed soap into the tub and stirred with both hands. Foam swelled like a mountain above it. She sang, "Into the tub—bubbles pop!" His eyes grew round. "A mountain!"
"A bubble mountain has an order," Mom whispered. "Head tipped back, a bucket waterfall! Then water stays out of your eyes. Bubbles next, sparkle last!" Pipo stamped eagerly. "Then it will not sting?"

Pipo splashed into the tub. Head tipped back, Mom trickled water over it. No stinging eyes! Rubbing bubbles over himself made him fluffy as a lamb. He flicked bubbles with both hands. "Into the tub—bubbles pop!"
After rinsing, his fur felt fresh and soft. Not a scratchy bit remained. Crouching beside the tub with hands at his chest, he asked, "Getting into a tub was this fun?"
The next evening, when sheep entered the pen, Pipo ran to the tub first. "One, head back, bucket waterfall! Two, bubbles on, little lamb! Three, rinse and sparkle!" Mom smiled with the bucket.
Mom lifted Pipo high. "Soft as a lamb!" A bath felt like the most exciting water play instead of something scary. In her arms, he called, "Into the tub—bubbles pop!"
